    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D38", "R70"],
      "pins": ["D38.2", "D38.4", "R70.1", "R70.2"],
      "nets": ["Net-(D38-K2)", "NET0017"],
      "observed": "The green LED half of dual LED D38 has its anode A2 (pin 4) on NET0017, and its cathode K2 (pin 2) goes through R70 to R70.2, which is also on NET0017. Anode and cathode of the same LED are therefore shorted together through 130R, so no forward current can flow and the green indicator cannot light. The red half (K1 via R12 to GND) has its cathode on GND, so the two halves are not built alike.",
      "expected": "The cathode-side resistor of an indicator LED should return to GND (as R12 does for K1), or the anode should be on a separate driven or supply node, so the LED can conduct when the ESTOP line changes state.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D38\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R70\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R70\") (pin \"1\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R12\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R70 Net-_D38-K2_ NET0017 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The green indicator LED on D38 is permanently dark. It also places a 130R load between the ESTOP drive net and itself, so status feedback for that channel is lost.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["U57", "Q10", "R73"],
      "pins": ["U57.2", "U57.4", "Q10.1", "R73.2"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "Net-(Q10-G)"],
      "observed": "The buffer U57 (a 1G125-style part with /OE, A, GND, Y, VCC pins) has its A input (pin 2) tied to the +5V rail, while its Y output drives the gate of P-channel Q10. When enabled, Y is driven high, which keeps the P-channel Q10 off. The pull-up R73 also holds the gate high, so Q10 never turns on.",
      "expected": "For a P-channel switch that is enabled by an active /OE, the A input should be tied to GND so that Y pulls the gate low to turn Q10 on. Tying A to the rail, as used for the NMOS enable buffer U3, produces the opposite polarity here.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U57\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U57\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\") (pintype \"output\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q10\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"G\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R73\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The 5V_switched_CAN power path through Q10 can never be enabled by 5V_CAN_ENABLE. CAN transceiver power then depends only on the Q11 path, so the enable function is not implemented as designed.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R92"],
      "pins": ["R92.1", "R92.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R92 is labelled 24k in the schematic value and in the SPICE deck. Its part description and MPN, however, specify 24Ω (MPN FRC0805J240TSD, '24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor'). The value and the purchased part disagree by three orders of magnitude.",
      "expected": "The value field should match the stocked part. If a 24Ω part is intended, the value should read 24R; if 24k is intended, the MPN and description should be corrected.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R92\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"Description\") \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R92 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24Ω part is fitted, the bleed or balance path across the VOUTP/VOUTN rails is about 1000 times lower than the schematic intends. This loads the supply heavily and changes the rail behaviour.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist shows a shorted green LED on D38 (anode and cathode both on NET0017 via R70), a P-channel gate driver U57 with its enable input tied to the wrong rail, and an R92 value that conflicts with its stocked 24Ω part. The main concern is the D38 short, which is a concrete connectivity fault, but confidence is moderate because the design files may intend some of these arrangements."
}

anomalies.observed: The green LED half of dual LED D38 has its anode A2 (pin 4) on NET0017, and its cathode K2 (pin 2) goes through R70 to R70.2, which is also on NET0017. Anode and cathode of the same LED are therefore shorted together through 130R, so no forward current can flow and the green indicator cannot light. The red half (K1 via R12 to GND) has its cathode on GND, so the two halves are not built alike.
anomalies.expected: The cathode-side resistor of an indicator LED should return to GND (as R12 does for K1), or the anode should be on a separate driven or supply node, so the LED can conduct when the ESTOP line changes state.
anomalies.impact: The green indicator LED on D38 is permanently dark. It also places a 130R load between the ESTOP drive net and itself, so status feedback for that channel is lost.

anomalies.observed: The buffer U57 (a 1G125-style part with /OE, A, GND, Y, VCC pins) has its A input (pin 2) tied to the +5V rail, while its Y output drives the gate of P-channel Q10. When enabled, Y is driven high, which keeps the P-channel Q10 off. The pull-up R73 also holds the gate high, so Q10 never turns on.
anomalies.expected: For a P-channel switch that is enabled by an active /OE, the A input should be tied to GND so that Y pulls the gate low to turn Q10 on. Tying A to the rail, as used for the NMOS enable buffer U3, produces the opposite polarity here.
anomalies.impact: The 5V_switched_CAN power path through Q10 can never be enabled by 5V_CAN_ENABLE. CAN transceiver power then depends only on the Q11 path, so the enable function is not implemented as designed.

anomalies.observed: R92 is labelled 24k in the schematic value and in the SPICE deck. Its part description and MPN, however, specify 24Ω (MPN FRC0805J240TSD, '24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor'). The value and the purchased part disagree by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: The value field should match the stocked part. If a 24Ω part is intended, the value should read 24R; if 24k is intended, the MPN and description should be corrected.

evidence.quote: (field (name "Description") " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24Ω part is fitted, the bleed or balance path across the VOUTP/VOUTN rails is about 1000 times lower than the schematic intends. This loads the supply heavily and changes the rail behaviour.
